analysis:
Behavior change: SSDPrefixCachePolicy.swift (patch ~lines 116-176) adds completeCheckpointMaxStageBytes/Millis. Macs with physical memory >= 96 GiB now default complete-checkpoint maxReadBytes to 3 GiB and maxStageMillis to 2500 ms, up from 1 GiB and 1000 ms. SSDHybridCheckpointStoreFactory.swift (head lines 77-79) wires these into SSDHybridCheckpointStore config. Explicit DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_SSD_MAX_STAGE_MB/MS still win via the refactored configuredMax* helpers, and invalid values fall back to the defaults as before. Attention-block caches keep the old defaults. The docs diff in docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md (lines 231-232, 283) describes this and is consistent with the code.

Security assessment (T-041, TB-007): no change to AES-GCM/DBK3 crypto, HMAC lookup tags, TTL (still 1800 s), disk budget, write caps, scope salting or the KEK. At-rest exposure is unchanged in kind. The only effect is a larger transient restore reservation on large-memory machines, still governed by GlobalKVCacheBudget and the cooperative read budget; I found no remote-consumer-controlled amplification. Residual items for the next pass: confirm that the 3 GiB stage reservation on top of the slot grant cannot starve live serving (availability, T-010/T-029 class), and that the retry raw-byte ceiling in SSDCheckpointReadBudget scales sensibly. Neither is evidenced as a regression here. Unchanged callers and the budget implementation were not supplied.
